name: Salt pan ground (SS)
description:
Feelers' 128px floor for the Salt Pan, drifted over with fine sand. The pan used to be dark umber under a lattice of salt cracks, which read as a hex grid the moment it tiled; this is the same ground with the sun on it. `$sand` is lifted about a stop and a half — bright enough to be a desert rather than a cellar, and stopped there rather than higher because the pan's own roster is mid-brown: past this the bodies start to sit at the floor's own tone, and the survivor's blue falls under 3:1 against it.

What makes it sand and not dirt is grain under ripples. Five seeded scatter passes lay the grain — a dark bed, a pale bed, a warm mid, a cool shade and a sparse quartz glint — and over them run wind ripples: shallow arcs banded at -13 degrees, each one a wide lee band with the lit face inside it, so a ripple falls off rather than stopping the way a drawn line does. The light on them is `$chitin` and `$husk`, not `$sand.light`: the light ramp mixes toward white, and a sand highlight built that way comes out grey where sunlight on sand is golden. Under all of it, dune-scale swells in three concentric steps each — steps rather than a gradient, because the Phaser bake flattens a gradient to one flat colour.

The pan is still here, quieter: salt bloom where the crust shows through the drift, the field's own rust flecks so the two grounds read as one world, and two old antlion funnels — shallow dishes now, not the four hard pits, because a black hole is the one thing on a tile the eye can count, and counting it is seeing the grid.

It tiles on a torus: every part whose bounds cross an edge is emitted again 128px over, so a ripple that leaves the right edge arrives at the left and no seam or grain-free margin survives the tiling. Every coordinate is hand-listed, so the tile is pixel-stable.
